title: Candidate interview orbit — post-call debrief template
content:
Purpose
This lightweight template is intended for rapid asynchronous debriefs after candidate interviews — especially useful for remote panels and cross-functional loops where not everyone is available at the same time. Use for technical screens, system design, pairing sessions, and hiring manager debriefs.

When to use
- Rapid screens (30–45m) where we want a single consolidated signal within 48 hours.
- When panelists are distributed across timezones and can't meet live for a consensus call.
- To capture evidence and decisions for audit / calibration later.

Note to interviewer (quick):
- Fill this within 24 hours of interview.
- Use concrete evidence sentences (e.g., “implemented a lock-free ring buffer in the pairing task; asked clarifying Qs X/Y/Z”).
- If unsure about scoring, flag for hiring manager to escalate.

Pre-call checklist (interviewer)
- Confirm candidate identity + timezones.
- Read the shared prompt/assignment and previous notes (link below).
- Open recording + collaborative doc.
- Quick tech stack check: ensure editor, terminal, and loom/screen share ready.

Interview metadata (fill at top)
- Candidate name:
- Role / level applied:
- Interviewer name:
- Panel role (e.g., tech-screen, pairing, manager):
- Date/time (UTC):
- Interview format: pairing | take-home review | system-design | behavioral
- Recording link / recording id: 
- Assignment link / repo: 

Focus / brief for this loop
- One-line: what we told candidate we were evaluating (technical fundamentals, ownership, collaboration, etc.).

Observed evidence (write short bullet evidence — not generic descriptors)
- Technical fundamentals (algorithms/data structures, complexity reasoning): 
  * Evidence: (explicit code sample, whiteboard approach, follow-up questions asked by candidate)
- System design / architecture (if applicable):
  * Evidence: (tradeoffs candidate considered, sketch fidelity, capacity/cost reasoning)
- Coding/pairing session behavior: 
  * Evidence: (makes incremental edits, uses tests, communicates intent, recovers from bug)
- Ownership and product sense (for PM-adjacent/product folks):
  * Evidence: (asks about edge cases, prioritization, success metrics)
- Communication & collaboration: 
  * Evidence: (lists alternative approaches, invites feedback, receives suggestions)

Fast scoring (one-line each) — pick one: StrongY | SlightY | Neutral | SlightN | StrongN
- Technical: 
- System design / architecture: 
- Collaboration & communication: 
- Role-fit / ownership: 
- Overall recommendation: 

Scoring guidance (short)
- StrongY: clear, correct solutions with tradeoff reasoning and fast recovery from mistakes.
- SlightY: correct but incomplete or needs some mentorship; candidate shows trajectory.
- Neutral: mixed signals — borderline; requires hiring manager calibration.
- SlightN: clear gaps in fundamentals or ergonomics for the role.
- StrongN: candidate likely not a fit for the role at this level.

Evidence snippets (copy exact quotes / timestamps where possible)
- "Candidate: 'I’d choose a bloom filter here because...'" — 00:17:23
- "Candidate refactors to test-first approach when pairing" — 00:10:12

Red flags (check any that apply)
- [ ] Plagiarism / reuse without attribution on take-home
- [ ] Unable to reason about time/space complexity at expected level
- [ ] Poor cross-team communication examples
- [ ] Misaligned ownership / soft-skills for role
- [ ] Hard blocker (missing required language / system experience)

Bias-aware note (required)
- Call out any hallmarks that might be culturally-specific (interruptions, accent, speaking style). Focus on decision-relevant evidence, not style.

Hiring decision & rationale (short paragraph)
- Recommendation: HIRE / NEXT-STEP (onsite / manager call / take-home) / DECLINE / HOLD
- Rationale: one crisp paragraph that ties evidence to the decision. If recommending hire, include level suggestion and initial ramp focus.

Admin checklist (post-decision)
- If HIRE -> send template offer checklist to recruiting: suggested base, sign-on, relocation? required approvals (list).
- If NEXT-STEP -> specify the next interviewer, timing window, and prompt.
- If DECLINE -> note feedback summary, who will close the loop with candidate.

Calibration signals (for hiring manager)
- Did the candidate exceed expectations in any specific axis? If yes, call out.
- Known tradeoffs vs role expectations (e.g., strong pragmatic engineer but less infra depth).

Evidence log (short table-style bullets)
- Ticket/PR references discussed by candidate: (PR# or link)
- Take-home file names:
- Pairing artifacts: (file or gist link)

Open questions & next steps (notes to HM/recruiter)
- Questions to follow up with candidate (salary, team comp, commute, offer timeline).
- Technical clarifications required? (e.g., confirm experience with X)

Appendix: templated language for candidate feedback (brief)
- If DECLINE: "We appreciated your time and the clarity you brought to X. At this time we’re not moving forward; primary gap: Y. We’ll keep your profile in our active pipeline for Z months."
- If NEXT-STEP: "We’d like to invite you to the next step: [pairing / manager call]. Estimated timeline: 7 days."

Notes to self (interviewer hacks)
- When pressed for time, fill scoring first and paste two evidence bullets. The hiring manager can expand later.
- Use timestamps to accelerate recall — helps SRE and calibration later.

References / links
- Hiring playbook (confluence): CONFLUENCE-12345://hiring/scorecards
- Interviewer training deck: slack://files/training/interviewer-primer.pdf

Unresolved items (for talent-ops)
- Should we require explicit transcript capture for remote loops? (pros/cons)
- How long should asynchronous debrief be editable? Current suggestion: 72h then locked for audit.

Version history (brief)
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Maya Patel)
- 2025-11-07: added scoring guidance + bias-aware note (Priya Desai)
- 2025-11-10: minor wording + linked artifacts update (Ethan Rivera)

-- end of template --

Quick usage examples (copy-paste snippets)
- One-line hire rationale for offer email: "Recommend hire, L3 IC — strong coding fundamentals, solid product judgment; initial focus: infra cleanup and mentoring."

- Manager follow-up prompt: "Focus next call on ownership and cross-team communication; ask for two examples of leading a cross-functional launch."

TODO (followups for people-ops)
- Create a short Loom walking new interviewers through this template (2–3m).
- Add quick-link buttons in Greenhouse to open this template pre-populated with candidate metadata.
- Decide on locking policy for debriefs (72h vs 7d).
